rangesFor: Dynamic TGA at about 10 K/min. Temperatures are the DTG peak of a step, in degrees C.

events.name: Loss of adsorbed moisture and volatile solvents
events.notes: Usually the first, small step. Strongly bound water can come off higher (see bound water).

events.name: Loss of bound or crystal water (hydrates)
events.notes: Hydrates often lose water in several steps; this overlaps with moisture loss and early organic loss.

events.name: Decomposition of organic capping agents or plant-extract biomolecules
events.notes: Broad and often several overlapping steps. In air the organic residue burns off, which can also add an exotherm in DSC.

events.name: Polymer degradation
events.notes: Depends strongly on the polymer type. In air degradation usually starts lower than in an inert gas.

events.name: Dehydroxylation of a metal hydroxide (loss of water from OH groups)
events.notes: The temperature depends on the metal. The mass loss can be compared with the theoretical value in the next section.

events.name: Decomposition of a nitrate precursor (loses water, NOx and oxygen)
events.notes: Hydrated nitrates lose water first, so the nitrate step often follows a water step.

events.name: Decomposition of an acetate precursor
events.notes: May leave a carbonate or carbon-containing intermediate that decomposes at a higher temperature.

events.name: Decomposition of a carbonate (loses CO2)
events.notes: Alkaline-earth carbonates decompose at the high end of this range; transition-metal carbonates lower.

events.name: Oxidation of carbon (soot, char or carbonaceous residue)
events.notes: Only possible when oxygen is present (air or oxygen). In nitrogen or argon the carbon stays as residue.
